In particular, rate-distortion theory has been proposed as a tool for handling the complexity and scale of real-world learning problems [13], [2], though concrete algorithmic mechanisms for leveraging it have been limited. One line of research addresses the algorithmic challenge by integrating rate-distortion ideas with Thompson Sampling [14]." — This identifies a gap ("concrete algorithmic mechanisms for leveraging it have been limited"), which could be seen as implicit positioning, but it doesn't explicitly state the paper's contribution or position. It's describing the literature and a gap, but not saying "our paper addresses this gap" or "in contrast to X, we...". Hmm, this is debatable. The gap statement could be considered a positioning statement in some interpretations. But strictly, the criterion says "states the contribution of the paper and/or its position among the literature". A gap statement alone doesn't state the paper's position unless it's connected to the paper's contribution. The paragraph ends with "One line of research addresses the algorithmic challenge by integrating rate-distortion ideas with Thompson Sampling [14]." — this is still describing other work.

Paragraph 3: Describes the Blahut-Arimoto algorithm and its utility. No contribution/positioning statement.
